❯ Write a 1500-word story about a lighthouse keeper. No tools.                                                                                                       

⏺ The Keeper of Orrin's Rock

  The light on Orrin's Rock had been lit every night for ninety-one years, and for the last thirty of them, it had been lit by Hester Quill.
  
  She arrived on the island in the autumn she turned forty-four, on the supply boat that came every six weeks, carrying a canvas duffel, a box of tinned peaches, and
  a letter from the Lighthouse Board that said her late uncle's post was hers to take or refuse. She had not planned to take it. She had been a bookkeeper in
  Harrowgate, and before that a girl in a town where the sea was something you looked at from a train. But the letter was dated the week after her divorce was
  finalized, and the room she had been renting had a window that faced a brick wall, and so she had said yes to the lighthouse the way some people say yes to a dare.
  
  The island was less than four acres of black stone and wind-scoured grass. There was the tower, white once and now the colour of old piano keys. There was the
  keeper's cottage, two rooms and a kitchen with a stove that smoked when the wind came from the north. There was a boathouse, a cistern, a small walled garden where
